newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Shenzhen B shares end higher despite crackdown.
newsitem.headline: Shenzhen B shares end higher despite crackdown.

text.p: Shenzhen's B share index ended sharply higher on Monday despite the latest crackdown on mainland Chinese buying new B shares, brokers said.
The China Securities newspaper said on Saturday that the Shanghai and Shenzhen bourses had banned mainland Chinese from buying new foreign currency B shares.

The newspaper said the two exchanges in separate notices issued on Friday said that existing investors must not buy any new B shares with immediate effect. But the exchanges did not set a deadline for them to unwind their existing positions.
The class B index rallied 1.96 points, or 2.24 percent, to close at 89.32, after hitting an intraday low of 86.02. Turnover expanded to HK$29.64 million from HK$8.96 million on Friday.
Analysts said Chinese investors felt quite calm about the news as rumours on the crackdown had circulated in the market for a long time.
Chinese investors are unlikely to sell their shares at current levels but will hold their positions over the long term until the market picks up, they said.
The rally on Monday was mainly linked to bargain-hunting by some overseas individual investors, a broker at China Southern Securities said.

Television tube producer SEG was the most actively-traded B share counter, rising HK$0.09 to HK$2.79 on volume of 1.50 million shares. The issue's advance was fueled by overseas institutional buying, the same broker said.

Textile issue Victor Onward was the sharpest gainer, surging HK$0.69, or 42.86 percent, to HK$2.30 on trade of 48,430 shares. But brokers said the counter would fall back in the coming sessions in light of the thin volume.

Property concern Vanke put on HK$1.00, or 28.57 percent, to HK$4.50 after 99,100 shares changed hands. There had been unconfirmed reports that some of Vanke's real estate projects in Shenzhen are being sold smoothly, brokers said.

Appliance maker Tsann Kuen climbed HK$0.24, or 10.21 percent, to HK$2.59. Health Mineral Water put on HK$0.18, or 7.83 percent, to HK$2.48 due to investor optimism over the issue's results this year, brokers said.
Diesel engine Changchai maintained its downward trend, falling HK$0.06 to HK$5.00 on heavy trade of 1.36 million shares. Brokers gave no reason for the decline.
The class A market edged higher on Monday, with sentiment boosted by strong gains posted by the Shanghai A market, brokers said.
But there were signs that some funds had flowed out of Shenzhen into Shanghai, where there were rumours of possible changes to the Shanghai bourse's leadership, brokers said.

The A share index inched up 0.45 point, or 0.17 percent, to finish at 267.00 on turnover of 3.41 billion yuan, compared with 3.47 billion yuan the previous session. The composite index gained 0.76 point, or 0.30 percent, to close at 252.66.
Wuhan Department Store was the biggest A share gainer, surging 0.73 yuan, or 11.20 percent, to 7.25 yuan.
